props.gloss_en: the mishnah: from when does one mention the might of rain? -- the wording the Gemara probes at 2a.4 and 2a.8
the tanna stands there -- on the Berakhot mishnah, which teaches that the might of rain is mentioned
one mentions the might of rain in [the blessing of] the resurrection of the dead
and one requests [rain] in the blessing of the years
and havdala in 'who graciously grants knowledge'
rather, the tanna came up from Rosh HaShana: having taught 'on the Chag they are judged for water', he taught 'from when does one mention the might of rain'
and on the Chag [the world] is judged for water
R' Yochanan: [it says 'might of rain'] because they fall with might
as it is said: 'Who does great things beyond searching out, marvels without number' (Job 5:9)
and it is written: 'Who gives rain upon the earth and sends water upon the fields' (Job 5:10)
Rabba bar Sheila: of the creation it is written 'His discernment is beyond searching out' (Isa 40:28), and 'Who sets firm the mountains with His strength, girded with might' (Ps 65:7)
[the mention of rain is] in prayer -- the din whose source the stam asks
the baraita: 'to love the Lord your God and to serve Him with all your heart' (Deut 11:13) -- which is service in the heart? that is prayer
R' Yochanan: three keys are in the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, that were not given over to an agent
the key of rain
the key of birthing
and the key of the resurrection of the dead
the key of rain -- as it is written: 'the Lord will open for you His good treasure, the heavens, to give the rain of your land in its season' (Deut 28:12)
the key of birthing, whence? -- as it is written: 'and God remembered Rachel... and He opened her womb' (Gen 30:22)
the key of the resurrection, whence? -- as it is written: 'and you shall know that I am the Lord when I open your graves' (Ezek 37:13)
in the West they say: also the key of livelihood
as it is written: 'You open Your hand [and satisfy every living thing]' (Ps 145:16)
[R' Yochanan] would tell you: rain is [the same as] livelihood

schemas.gloss_en: אתיא חקר חקר מברייתו של עולם: 'ad ein cheker' of rain (Job 5:9) and 'ein cheker litvunato' of creation (Isa 40:28); of creation it is written 'girded with might' (Ps 65:7) -- so rain too is an act of might
וכתיב בתריה: ונתתי מטר ארצכם בעתו יורה ומלקוש (Deut 11:14) -- written right after 'serve Him with all your heart' = prayer, so rain belongs in prayer

supports.gloss_en: דקתני: מזכירים גבורות גשמים בתחיית המתים... וקתני מאימתי -- the Berakhot mishnah teaches THAT one mentions, and this one teaches from WHEN
דתנן: ובחג נידונין על המים -- and having taught that, he taught מאימתי
דתניא: ולעבדו בכל לבבכם -- איזו היא עבודה שבלב? הוי אומר זו תפלה

objections.gloss_en: וליתני התם! מאי שנא דשבקיה עד הכא? -- if the tanna stands on the Berakhot mishnah, let him teach this there; why leave it until here?
מאי משמע? -- how do these verses imply that rain is an act of might?

answered_by.gloss_en: אתיא חקר חקר מברייתו של עולם -- the gezera shava gs_cheker_cheker

objections.gloss_en: ורבי יוחנן מאי טעמא לא קא חשיב להא? -- why does R' Yochanan count three and omit the key of livelihood?

answered_by.gloss_en: אמר לך: גשמים היינו פרנסה (= p_geshamim_hainu_parnasa, attributed to R' Yochanan)
